# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Mar 1 - 7, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on refining the protocol's technical debt and aligning the Kona stack with existing node specifications. Significant effort was directed toward triaging older issues and deprecating outdated feature requests, such as Flashblocks support in Geth, following shifts in the `op-geth` architecture. Active technical discussions centered on resolving discrepancies between Kona and `op-node`, specifically regarding data derivation and frame parsing, to ensure protocol consistency across the Superchain.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new pull requests were merged during this period, the week was characterized by intensive technical planning and alignment on the following fronts:

### Kona Protocol Alignment
Development efforts focused on resolving critical discrepancies between the Kona implementation and the standard `op-node` behavior. Key areas of focus included:
*   **Data Derivation:** Addressing orphaned sources in `kona-derive` and resolving disagreements regarding brotli channels.
*   **Protocol Security:** Planning fixes for a denial-of-service vulnerability in `kona-protocol` related to unknown batch types.
*   **Parsing Consistency:** Investigating mismatches in Kona frame parsing to ensure seamless interoperability.

### L2CM Access Control
The team explored enhancements to the Layer 2 Config Manager (L2CM) by proposing the addition of `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` access control to predeploy `initialize()` functions. This work aims to standardize security patterns across L1 and L2 contracts.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw a concerted effort to clean up the repository's backlog and address emerging protocol bugs.

*   **Closed Issues:**
    *   **Deprecations:** Issue [#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/756) regarding Flashblocks support was closed due to the deprecation of `op-geth`, ensuring the design docs remain aligned with current engineering priorities.
    *   **General Maintenance:** Two legacy bug reports ([#338](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/338) and [#339](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/339)) were resolved and closed.

*   **Active Issues:**
    *   **Kona Stability:** Multiple high-priority issues are currently being tracked to bring Kona into parity with the OP Stack specification, including [#19340](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19340) (orphaned sources), [#19333](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19333) (brotli channel disagreements), and [#19335](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19335) (frame parsing).
    *   **Security:** Issue [#19334](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19334) remains a focus for mitigating potential DoS vectors within the protocol.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was highlighted by proactive community engagement in the Kona ecosystem. Contributor **Moses-main** was particularly active, volunteering to tackle several complex protocol discrepancies and security vulnerabilities. There is also evidence of strong cross-project coordination, as seen in discussions between **ajsutton** and **maurelian**, who provided guidance on aligning L2 access control implementations with existing L1 contract patterns. This indicates a healthy, peer-review-driven environment focused on maintaining high security and architectural standards across the Superchain.
